question: Who among the following passed the widow remarriage Act in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Canning**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Canning** passed the Widow Remarriage Act in India.
 
• The Widow Remarriage Act, also known as Act XV of 1856, was enacted on 26th July 1856.
 
• This act provided legal sanction to the remarriage of Hindu widows, which was previously prohibited by societal norms and religious practices.
 
• The act was a significant social reform aimed at improving the status and rights of women in India during the British colonial period.
 
• It played a crucial role in the broader movement for women's rights and social reform in 19th century India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Canning** served as the Governor-General of India from 1856 to 1862.
 
• He was also the first Viceroy of India after the transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown following the Revolt of 1857.
 
• Lord Canning is known for his efforts to implement social reforms and his role in the reorganization of the administration after the revolt.
 
• The Widow Remarriage Act was part of a broader set of reforms aimed at improving the social and legal status of various marginalized groups in Indian society.
 
• Other notable figures who supported the act included Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, who was a prominent social reformer advocating for the rights of women and widows.
